subject: radiology
title: Gastrointestinal bleeding embolisation

steps.tx: Imaging finds the bleeding point before any catheter is moved. **CT angiography** in the arterial phase shows active extravasation above roughly half a millilitre per minute. **Catheter angiography** then confirms the site with a selective blush, pseudoaneurysm or abrupt vessel cutoff. A negative map with continuing bleeding can still justify **empiric embolisation** of the likely bed. Provocative clot stirring is avoided outside studies because it risks losing control of bleeding.
steps.say: Imaging finds the bleeding point before any catheter is moved. CT angiography shows active leakage and guides the catheter correctly. Selective angiography then confirms a blush or abrupt cutoff clearly. Continuing bleeding with a negative map can still justify treatment of the likely bed in unstable patients.

steps.tx: The axial arterial phase CT shows a bright **contrast extravasation blush** spilling inside a bowel loop in the left abdomen. A white **mesenteric feeding artery** runs towards the blush and names the territory for catheterisation. This single image localises active bleeding before any catheter is advanced. Examiners expect this map first because it shortens procedure time and reduces **non target embolisation** risk.
steps.say: The axial CT is diagnostic because a bright blush spills inside a bowel loop. A mesenteric feeding artery runs towards the blush and names the territory. This image localises active bleeding before any catheter is advanced. Examiners expect this map first because it shortens the procedure and reduces unnecessary embolisation.

vis.alt: Axial arterial phase CT angiogram showing active bowel contrast extravasation and feeding mesenteric artery.
vis.caption: Arterial CT shows active intraluminal contrast blush from mesenteric branch. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Upper gut arteries tolerate embolisation because rich collateral arcades protect tissue. **Gastroduodenal sandwich coils** block both ends because pancreaticoduodenal arcades refill a single sided block. **Left gastric embolisation** calms diffuse fundal oozing when endoscopy fails repeatedly. Mesenteric branches need a superselective tip because **vasa recta** are end arteries with little collateral supply. Empiric treatment without a seen blush suits unstable patients who rebleed after failed endoscopy.
steps.say: Upper gut arteries are tolerant of embolisation because collateral arcades protect tissue well. Gastroduodenal coils block both ends because arcades refill single blocks. Left gastric treatment calms diffuse fundal oozing after endoscopy fails. Mesenteric branches need superselective tips because their small branches are end arteries with little collateral supply.

steps.tx: Bowel infarction is the feared price of poorly placed embolisation. A block placed too proximally infarcts a long bowel segment, so the tip advances beyond **marginal arcades**. New pain with rising lactate and peritonism after the procedure suggests **bowel infarction** and needs surgical review. **Coils** are favoured over particles in bowel beds because particles shower too widely. A stricture months later marks healed ischaemia and needs endoscopic surveillance.
steps.say: Bowel infarction is the feared price of poorly placed embolisation. A proximal block infarcts a long segment, so the tip advances distally. New pain with rising lactate suggests infarction and needs surgical review. Coils are favoured over particles because particles shower too widely, while late stricture marks healed ischaemia.

vis.alt: Diagram showing bowel arterial supply. Illustrates how superselective embolization distal to marginal arcades preserves collateral flow, preventing extensive bowel ischemia compared to proximal embolization.
vis.caption: Superselective embolization preserves marginal arcade flow, preventing bowel ischemia

steps.tx: Rebleeding after gut embolisation follows a protocol rather than panic. **Repeat angiography** remaps the territory first because new feeders often replace sealed vessels. Surgical backup is warned early for ischaemic or uncontrollable cases rather than called late. **Acid suppression** and transfusion continue alongside radiology and are never paused for the procedure. Every death after gut embolisation is reviewed so mapping and selection lessons improve future care.
